en: I grew up in a family where history sat at the dinner table. All his life, my father engaged in a number of parallel professional activities, none of which alone defined him, but most of which were steeped in his love of history. I was in my teens when he started a regular program on Haitian television that explored little-known details of the history of the country. That program rarely surprised me: the stories my dad told his audience were not different from those he told at home. I had catalogued some of them on the yellowed cards that embodied a massive biographical dictionary of Haitian history my father never finished. Later, in the class he taught in world history in my high school, I worked harder than my classmates to earn a passing grade. But his lectures, good as they were, never matched what I learned at home on Sundays.
zh: 我在一个历史坐在餐桌旁的家庭里长大。父亲一生从事过多种并行的职业活动，没有哪一种单独定义了他，但其中大多浸透着他对历史的热爱。我十几岁时，他在海地电视台开办了一个定期节目，发掘这个国家历史上鲜为人知的细节。那节目很少让我惊讶：父亲讲给观众的故事，和他在家讲的并无二致。我曾把其中一些故事编目在泛黄的卡片上，那些卡片承载着一部庞大的海地历史人物传记辞典——父亲从未完成它。后来，他就在我就读的高中教世界史，为了及格，我比同学们都用功。但他的课讲得再好，也比不上我星期天在家里学到的东西。

en: Sunday afternoon was when my father's brother, my uncle Hénock, came to visit. He was one of the few people I knew who actually earned a living from knowing history. He was nominally the director of the National Archives, but writing was his true passion and he published historical research too fast for most readers to keep up with—in books, journals, and newspapers, at times his preferred medium. On Sundays, he tested his ideas on my dad, for whom history was increasingly becoming only a favorite hobby as his law practice expanded. The brothers disagreed more often than not, in part because they genuinely saw the world quite differently, in part because the heat of their divergences, both political and philosophical, fueled their ceremonial of love.
zh: 星期天下午，父亲的兄弟、我的叔叔埃诺克（Hénock）会来做客。他是我认识的人中少数真正靠懂历史谋生的人之一。他名义上是国家档案馆馆长，但写作才是他真正的热情所在；他发表历史研究的速度快得让大多数读者跟不上——专著、期刊、报纸，报纸有时还是他偏爱的媒介。星期天，他拿我父亲检验自己的想法；随着律师业务扩展，历史对父亲来说越来越只是一项心爱的业余爱好。兄弟俩多半话不投机，部分因为他们确实以很不同的方式看世界，部分因为他们政治与哲学分歧的热度，恰好为他们的爱的仪式提供了燃料。

en: Sunday afternoon was ritual time for the Trouillot brothers. History was their alibi for expressing both their love and their disagreements—with Hénock overplaying his bohemian side and my father stressing bourgeois rationality. They argued about long-dead figures, Haitian and foreign, the way one chats about neighbors—with the concerned distance that comes from knowing intimate details of the lives of people who are not family.
zh: 星期天下午是特鲁约兄弟的仪式时间。历史是他们表达爱与分歧的托词——埃诺克尽情扮演他的波希米亚气质，父亲则强调资产阶级的理性。他们争论早已作古的海地和外国人物，就像人们闲聊邻居——带着那种关切的距离感：你熟知一些并非家人者的生活细节，才会有这种距离。

en: Were I not suspicious of obvious genealogies, I could claim this mixture of intimacy and distance, and the class, race, and gender positions that made it possible, as the central part of my intellectual heritage. But I have learned on my own that the point about such claims may be less what they assert than the fact of their assertion. Growing up who I was, I could not escape historicity, but I also learned that anyone anywhere with the right dosage of suspicion can formulate questions to history with no pretense that these questions themselves stand outside history.
zh: 倘若我不是对显明的谱系心存怀疑，我本可以把这种亲密与距离的混合，以及使之成为可能的阶级、种族与性别位置，认作我知识遗产的核心部分。但我自己已经懂得：这类宣称的要点，与其说在于它断言了什么，不如说在于它被断言这一事实本身。以我的身份长大，我逃不开历史性；但我也懂得，任何地方的任何人，只要带着恰当剂量的怀疑，都能向历史提出问题，而无需假装这些问题本身站在历史之外。

en: Long before I read Nietzsche's Untimely Meditations, I knew intuitively that people can suffer from historical overdose, complaisant hostages of the pasts they create. We learned that much in many Haitian households at the peak of the Duvaliers' terror, if only we dared to look outside. Yet being who I am and looking at the world from there, the mere proposition that one could—or should—escape history seems to me either foolish or deceitful. I find it hard to harness respect for those who genuinely believe that postmodernity, whatever it may be, allows us to claim no roots. I wonder why they have convictions, if indeed they have any. Similarly, allegations that we have reached the end of history or that we are somewhat closer to a future when all pasts will be equal make me wonder about the motives of those who make such claims. I am aware that there is an inherent tension in suggesting that we should acknowledge our position while taking distance from it, but I find that tension both healthy and pleasant. I guess that, after all, I am perhaps claiming that legacy of intimacy and estrangement.
zh: 早在读尼采《不合时宜的沉思》（Untimely Meditations）之前，我就凭直觉知道，人会因历史过量而受害，成为自己所创造的那些过去的温顺人质。在杜瓦利埃家族恐怖统治的顶点，许多海地家庭都懂得了这一点——只要我们敢于朝外面看。然而，作为我这样的人、从那里看世界，“人能够——或者应该——逃离历史”这个命题本身，在我看来不是愚蠢就是欺骗。我很难对那些真心相信后现代性（无论它是什么）允许我们宣称没有根的人保持敬意。我纳闷他们为什么会有信念——如果他们真有的话。同样，声称我们已经到达历史终结、或声称我们离一切过去都将平等的未来更近了一步，这类说法让我怀疑提出它们的人的动机。我知道，主张我们应当承认自己的位置、同时又与之保持距离，这里面有一种内在的张力；但我觉得这种张力既健康又令人愉悦。我想，说到底，我或许还是在认领那份亲密与疏离的遗产。

en: We are never as steeped in history as when we pretend not to be, but if we stop pretending we may gain in understanding what we lose in false innocence. Naiveté is often an excuse for those who exercise power. For those upon whom that power is exercised, naiveté is always a mistake.
zh: 我们假装不在历史之中时，恰恰最深地浸在历史里；但如果我们停止假装，我们在理解上的所得，或许能补偿我们在虚假无辜上的所失。天真往往是掌权者的借口。对于被权力施加于身的人，天真永远是一个错误。

en: This book is about history and power. It deals with the many ways in which the production of historical narratives involves the uneven contribution of competing groups and individuals who have unequal access to the means for such production. The forces I will expose are less visible than gunfire, class property, or political crusades. I want to argue that they are no less powerful.
zh: 这本书谈的是历史与权力。它处理的是历史叙述生产中的种种方式：相互竞争的群体与个人对这种生产贡献不均，因为他们接近生产手段的机会并不平等。我要揭示的力量，不如炮火、阶级财产或政治运动那样显眼。我要论证的是，它们的力量并不稍逊。

en: I also want to reject both the naive proposition that we are prisoners of our pasts and the pernicious suggestion that history is whatever we make of it. History is the fruit of power, but power itself is never so transparent that its analysis becomes superfluous. The ultimate mark of power may be its invisibility; the ultimate challenge, the exposition of its roots.
zh: 我还要拒绝两种说法：一是天真的命题——我们是自己过去的囚徒；二是有害的暗示——历史不过是我们随意造就的东西。历史是权力的果实，但权力本身从来不是透明到无需分析的地步。权力最深刻的标记或许是它的不可见；而最艰巨的挑战，则是揭示它的根柢。
